Podium is the all-in-one AI-powered lead management and communication platform used by more than 100,000 businesses to acquire and convert new customers. At the forefront of Podium’s innovation is its AI employee, who ensures businesses respond to leads instantly, anytime of the day or night—significantly increasing lead conversion rates and revenue.
Podium helps businesses obtain more reviews, rank higher on Google, and consolidate lead channels. Businesses can call and text customers from the web and/or mobile app, send payment links, drive repeat business through bulk messages, and more—all managed and delivered from one easy-to-use dashboard. Additionally, with Podium’s AI Employee and automations, businesses can efficiently handle customer inquiries seamlessly across all communication channels, providing timely and accurate responses that drive sales.
Podium’s innovative work has gained recognition on top industry lists, such as Forbes’ Next Billion Dollar Startups, Forbes’ Cloud 100, the Inc. 5000, and Fast Company’s World’s Most Innovative Companies.
Podium was founded in 2014 and is headquartered in Lehi, Utah. It is currently backed by Accel, Summit Partners, GV (formerly Google Ventures), and Y Combinator.

content.description:
The iSono Health platform combines automated 3D ultrasound technology with cloud computation and artificial intelligence to empower women and their physicians with early detection and monitoring of breast cancer. Our patented compact ultrasound scanner captures 3D images through automatic scanning of whole breast volume in 1 min. The device connects to a smartphone/tablet/laptop and is controlled by our mobile app. The data is transferred to a secure cloud for image processing and storage. Our machine learning algorithm uses acoustic biomarkers to identify abnormal masses.  Our platform’s automated operation and software expands ultrasound use in point-of-care diagnostics as well as monitoring of breast health at home, walk-in and mobile clinics. 

iSono Health offers women and healthcare providers :
Safety: No Radiation
Actionable Feedback with AI
Fast: 2min Scan
Easy to Use

content.description:
At Resolve we’re accelerating construction to build as fast as the future demands. Construction projects are all slowed down by rework that arises after humans spot issues in real life that slipped through all the hours of design reviews and coordination. Resolve enables construction teams to detect these issues in 3D BIM as early as possible so that we can close the gap between design and reality.

By combining realtime collaboration in the web, immersive VR reviews, and AI-driven spatial navigation into the most easy to use platform for BIM reviews, Resolve empowers construction teams to identify risks earlier, coordinate faster, and deliver higher-quality assets across mission-critical infrastructure.

Resolve has been used to deliver over 6GW of data center capacity and on projects across pharma, water treatment, healthcare, and other critical assets.

content.description:
CareMessage is a social enterprise and the largest patient engagement platform for low-income populations in the United States. We deliver personalized health education and care coordination through text messaging — reaching patients where they already are, in the language they speak, at the moments that matter most. Unlike technology built for large health systems and adapted down, CareMessage is designed from the ground up for organizations serving low-income, historically marginalized communities.

Founded in 2012, CareMessage has now engaged more than 22 million people across 45 states, partnering with Federally Qualified Health Centers, Free and Charitable Clinics, and Tribal Health Organizations to produce measurable improvements in health equity — and we publish the evidence to prove it. As a nationally-recognized social enterprise we reinvest revenue into impact. We believe driving profit and purpose are not trade-offs, they are the same strategy.

CareMessage has been recognized by TIME 100 Most Influential Company for Impact in Equality, Inc. Best in Business for Social Good, and recognized at the World Economic Forum for Social Entrepreneurship. Learn more about our work at: www.caremessage.org/impact

content.description:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

We’re starting in hotels. Every day, housekeeping teams move linens between floors, restock carts, and fold stacks of laundry before the next guests arrive. It’s physical work that has to get done every shift.

Our first robot, Vibe 01, folds a hand towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds. It learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations. We’re piloting Vibe 01 at a Hilton property and working with hotels under the Marriott, Hilton, and IHG brands to bring it to more locations.

Folding is the first job. Next are restocking housekeeping carts and moving linens between floors. We’re Archer, Daniel, Katherine, and Pranav, and we’re building robots that can learn to do routine physical work across industries.

content.description:
Luminary is an AI CEO that leads human and agent teams on company-wide missions. We're building the complete infrastructure for a fully AI-native company, starting with a world model of how your business works and building up to an AI CEO that can lead it.

Today's AI tools are good at automating the work they're handed, but they still wait to be told what to do next. So even with the abundance of AI agents, companies are still bottlenecked by leadership and vision. Someone has to decide what's worth building, rally the right people behind it, and bring it to market.

Luminary takes on that job. Instead of asking it to build a feature, you hand it part of your business to grow. It then proactively discovers opportunities, plans high-impact missions, and leads your people and its own agent swarms to accomplish them. 

Some examples of audacious missions it can execute:

- Launch a product: It spots customers building the same workaround, makes the business case, directs coding agents to build it, and rolls it out.
- Enter a new market: It finds an unexpected group of buyers, reworks positioning and pricing around them, and wins the first accounts.
- Rescue a stalled deal: It notices an enterprise deal losing momentum, designs a new strategy with your sales team, and gets it signed.

Under the hood, Luminary builds a living world model and follows a leadership constitution that shapes every call. Proprietary evals check every deliverable, and a recursive self-improvement loop turns each mission into institutional wisdom.

content.description:
Our mission is to rebuild the file system, the oldest idea in computing, for its newest users: AI agents.

FlashDrive is a shared drive for teams and their AI agents. You can use it via MCP or mount it like a normal folder on macOS and Linux, so your laptop, your teammates' and every sandbox work in the same live files at once. Agents hand off work through files: one writes, the next one reads.

That makes AI multiplayer across a whole company. Everyone keeps the agent they already like, whether that's Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or something custom, and there's no new app to learn. Your agents and your teammates' agents work in the same files and pick up where each other left off.

Shared drives were built for people. Agents work differently: many of them edit the same files at once. Unlike Dropbox or Google Drive, FlashDrive merges edits made at the same time, or keeps both, instead of creating a conflicted copy. Cloud sandboxes connect with no setup, huge files stream instead of filling the disk, and every file can be searched with keywords and grep.

(FlashDrive is by Evokoa, Inc.)
content.products_or_services: A shared drive for your team and all your AI agents.

content.description:
Tilo gives AI agents one shared computer. Today every agent gets its own virtual machine and works by screenshots and clicks, which is slow, expensive and brittle. Agents that work together have to describe what they did to each other in messages.

Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for agents as users. Every app exports typed actions that agents call over MCP while people use the same actions as buttons, on the same live state. Many agents work in one workspace at once and read each other's work instead of messaging about it. Every change is attributed and can be undone, and irreversible actions need permission. Because state and interface are separate, agents can generate an app's entire UI on demand.

On the same multi-app task with the same model, agents on Tilo were about 29× cheaper and 90× faster than computer use, which failed. A small model on Tilo did it for about 1/10,000 of the frontier model's cost. In our scale test, 50 agents worked in one shared workspace on a single laptop, at about 60 MB of memory per agent. Tilo runs headless, in our cloud, or as a desktop, and you can open any workspace from the browser.
content.products_or_services: The Microsoft of the AI era: the operating system for AI agents.

content.description:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.

content.description:
Frontrunner lets GTM teams describe the work they need done and deploy agents that run it, connected to their existing tools and data. Our customers are building agents for everything from inbound lead routing to signal-based outbound and multi-touch attribution. Think Cursor for GTM: the place to engineer your revenue factory. 

GTM engineers and rev ops teams spend their days stitching tools together; and fielding requests from sales and marketing. Each campaign has its own version of who the customer is, what makes a lead qualified, and which signals matter. When the business changes, someone has to update that logic everywhere. Even teams that can build their own tools end up depending on the person who built them to keep everything running.

Not only does Frontrunner give those agents a shared understanding of your ICP, customers, and gtm motion, but persists that shared understanding automatically when business context changes so that it remains in sync. Sales and marketing build, run, and manage agents against that shared context, using the tools they already know. As prospects move from first touch to closed deal, the results feed back into how agents target, qualify, and engage the next account. Your revenue factory gets smarter with every cycle, optimizing for conversion across the full sales journey.

Our customers range from AI native startups to agencies running GTM for their clients to established businesses supporting large sales teams. They use Frontrunner to turn their best plays into agents their whole team can use.

US workers' compensation paid out $64.1 billion in 2023. Personal injury, malpractice, and other insurance claims add billions more. Our agents reconstruct patient histories, reason across conflicting evidence, and produce defensible analyses, with every finding cited to the original record.

We've sold to physician expert witnesses and medical-legal firms, turning thousands of pages into court-ready chronologies an expert can verify in minutes. Next: TPAs and insurers, where the same review sits behind every injury claim.

content.description:
Axiomat makes it impossible for AI agents to make mistakes when querying a company’s data. It formally verifies that the agents’ queries are correct before employees or customers rely on the answers. 

It is becoming increasingly important for companies to rely on AI without the need for humans to manually check the answers. This has created a need for systems which can guarantee correctness without limiting the agent’s capabilities. Axiomat provides the infrastructure to prove that answers are correct, starting with data queries and analysis. It brings mathematical guarantees to the agents working with your data.

The team brings direct experience solving AI hallucinations through Ethan’s work as an Applied Scientist at AWS, where he worked on formally verifying AI responses. They also bring research experience in AI, LLMs, and formal methods from EPFL, the University of Toronto, and Georgia Tech.

content.description:
RouterPlus is a marketplace for AI inference. We find the right AI model for a team's product, then get it served at the team's scale, at the best price.

Most teams that run AI in production pay for a top model on every task, when a cheaper model can do most of the work. The same model can also cost twice as much depending on which provider runs it, and many providers fail at peak traffic.

RouterPlus tests models on a team's own traffic and recommends one. Providers then compete for the workload. We check that the chosen provider can hold the team's real peak, and we keep a second provider ready as a backup. Teams call the model through one API.

Our largest customer runs 3 million agent conversations a day on RouterPlus.

Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Engineers don’t have time to keep improving the agents they’ve shipped. Context bloat, chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, so no one can tell whether the agent is delivering the outcome it was built for.

Papaya analyzes production traces and code, groups runs by business use case, and measures each one against its intended business outcome. Over 200 research-backed analyses find what’s holding the agent back. Every fix is ranked by impact on quality, latency, and cost, and the ones engineers approve ship as pull requests. Customers typically see a 20%+ quality improvement from the first analysis.

content.description:
Latent automates post-training for LLMs. It reads signals inside a model as it works and labels every answer and agent step in milliseconds, so teams improve their models on their own production traffic instead of paying for human labeling.

The same signal works in real time. Latent lets an output through, holds it, re-asks a stronger model, or sends it to review with the reason attached. Reading the model is over 660x cheaper than running an LLM judge, so it can check everything. One voice AI company using Latent finds 98% of its agent’s failures by reviewing only the riskiest 43% of answers, and in testing Latent stopped 99% of rule-breaking agents before they acted, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge.

It works with self-hosted and API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, runs hosted or fully in your own cloud, and installs with one line of code.

content.description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype, and it’s being prepared to move a locomotive on battery power in the coming days.
content.products_or_services: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.

content.description:
Organizely helps American manufacturers use AI to lower production costs. 

Factories depend on three resources: materials, equipment, and labor. Costs rise unexpectedly when components are missing, machines go down, or staffing doesn’t match demand. We experienced this firsthand while owning and operating a factory in the U.S. for six years. As we scaled, it was expensive to resolve factory-wide bottlenecks quickly and it became harder to stay competitive on price. 

Other companies are trying to layer AI agents on top of legacy ERPs to do logistics work, but the underlying data architectures limit how much those agents can understand and do. So we’re building a new ERP from the ground up for the era of AI. 

Organizely is an AI-native ERP with AI reasoning and machine learning algorithms embedded throughout for a single intelligent platform that can model, predict, and act. We natively automate all core manufacturing workflows including demand planning, raw material tracking, machine maintenance, and production scheduling. 

Organizely continuously improves over time, suggesting new ways for manufacturers to reduce costs and produce more with their existing facilities and teams. It's the whole factory solved. 

We’ve deployed to factories across six U.S. states and now we’re bringing AI to all factories across America. 🇺🇸
content.products_or_services: A New AI-Native ERP for American Manufacturers 🇺🇸

content.description:
Archgen Labs builds AI-powered chip design tools for the next generation of 3D semiconductors.

Stacking compute vertically shortens connections and reduces the energy and delay of moving data. But it also makes heat harder to remove. Our tools help engineers optimize placement, timing, and temperature together so they can build faster, more power-efficient 3D chips.

Our GPU-accelerated placement engine ranked first in the Hudson River Trading macro-placement challenge. LayerTherm, our thermal analysis tool, predicts chip temperatures roughly 5,000× faster than conventional simulation in our benchmarks, helping engineers explore more designs and identify hotspots earlier. Newton, our AI chip design engineer, automates work across placement, routing, design-rule fixes, and timing closure.

We’re working with GlobalFoundries on 3D chip development, targeting our first tapeout in 2027.

content.description:
Construction projects lose money in the gap between what the documents say and what gets built. One missed discrepancy between the specs, drawings, geotechnical study and code can become a seven-figure claim eighteen months later.

Telamont catches contractual, technical and code-compliance risks in construction documents and gives teams the system to act on them before they become costly rework or disputes.

Telamont connects to where your documents live and pulls in every file and revision as it lands, continuously building a complete picture of the project. Every page is checked against the rest of the project, so risks are flagged as soon as they appear. Instead of reviewing documents, teams act on flagged risks, tracking each from detection to resolution while managing exposure and pursuing recovery opportunities across every project.

We're starting with process EPCs in oil and gas, chemicals, semiconductors, pharma, and food and beverage, then expanding into water and power.

content.description:
Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve.

Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. Each codebase has conventions, history, and failure modes that a general-purpose model doesn't know. We learn those continuously from the code, how the team works, and the mistakes agents make. Then we fix the codebase and add merge gates that use deterministic verifiers instead of another model's judgment, so the same mistake can't ship twice. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work.

We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.

content.description: At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility’s network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. Because the model sees every transformer, it will also help utilities decide when new wires are really needed, and how distribution load can free up transmission for new data centers. We’re working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.

Workers IO is building simulation environments to catch failures in mission-critical software before they reach production. We run your entire system through millions of simulated production scenarios to verify its correctness and performance properties.

For example, our reconciliation agents compare bank records with the fund administrator’s records and prepare the reconciliation for the finance team to review. People retain final sign-off, helping funds handle more operational work without adding headcount at the same pace.

Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI systems faster and keep them secure in production.

Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Armorer's detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks. Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won't feel the delay.

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS, including its first customer-facing AI security agent, which scaled to 100k+ customers. Armorer is backed by Paul Vixie, an internet pioneer inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2014.

content.description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

content.description:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

content.description:
Industrial and legacy enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected layers of systems. Automating this work has required an FDE services approach in the past, because so much of it is bespoke and company specific.

Faraday is a self-improving platform that take on this operational work. It connects to their existing software and machines and automatically builds RL environments around each company’s workflows and data. Each job the agents do is checked against those environments, and the results are used to train them. The agents get better on their own with no additional work.

Continuous learning turns each company’s expertise into a compounding asset. Completed work, corrections, and employee feedback improve the agents, and those improvements carry into future jobs. The business preserves its knowledge while becoming more capable over time.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.

content.description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to.

In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute.

Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. Training an open model on our environments raised its full-solve rate on unseen tasks by 54% (from 25.6% to 39.5%), with no loss on general benchmarks. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that keeps AI climbing the frontier, long past human level in the real world.

content.description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

content.description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.

With tools like Cursor and Claude Code, writing software is no longer the bottleneck. Debugging is. Agents cannot fix production crashes using logs and traces that were sized for human eyeballs. The gap is missing data.

HyperProbe allows agents to debug live software autonomously. Our SDK drops non-breaking probes straight into running services to read exact variable states from memory at the moment of failure, instead of reasoning backwards from flat logs.

Zero redeploys. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction.

We turn 4-hour production war rooms into 10-minute automated resolutions. As agents write and operate more of the world's software, HyperProbe is the runtime observability layer that lets them understand what they built.

An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step.

We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company’s policies and interests, the agent’s current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Access is specific to the task at hand and reassessed as the agent works.

Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models to power their agents. They’ll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. Decawork is building those models.

content.description:
​Gamgee began with Rosie, founder Paul Conyngham’s dog. After surgery, chemotherapy and immunotherapy failed, Rosie was given months to live. Paul used AI and genomic analysis to identify targets in her tumour, then worked with scientists at UNSW to produce what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine delivered to a dog. Following treatment, several tumours shrank significantly and her quality of life improved

Gamgee is building an end to end platform for personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs. We sequence a dog’s tumour and healthy DNA, identify mutations unique to its cancer, and design a vaccine that teaches the immune system what to attack. We manage the entire process- from vet intake and tissue collection through genomic analysis, vaccine production, treatment and response monitoring

​We are now turning that one off effort into a repeatable clinical system. Gamgee is running clinical trials in Australia, working with vets, oncologists and specialised laboratories, and accepting cases globally. Our goal is to make personalised cancer treatment accessible to every dog that needs it- and use each case to improve the treatment for the next

content.description:
Fabraix builds state-of-the-art AI red-teaming agents that continuously detect security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI. Our product, Nyx, has already found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 companies. 

AI agents can change more often than teams can test them. A new model, prompt, tool, permission, or data source can change what an agent does, even when the application code stays the same. And AI is also increasing how much software companies produce and how often it changes. We built Nyx to automate the work required to red-team AI agents. It is multi modal by design and interacts with the target indirectly through controlled replicas of SaaS products and websites that we maintain, placing malicious payloads in webpages, documents, files, messages, and tool outputs to test how an agent behaves under different conditions.

We're also the team behind ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a benchmark that measures AI security in terms of how much it costs attackers to break an AI system; providing a game-theoretic framework to understand how motivated a rational attacker would be in exploiting the system.

content.description:
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build or operate things can see what each production run, load and job actually cost.

These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads.

So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter?

Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. 

Definite started in a plant office an hour from campus, watching a controller rebuild the same spreadsheet she rebuilds every month to tie her production system to her ledger. The three of us met at the University of Waterloo and had each spent our careers on a version of that join. Gurshabd built wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo, where proving customer assets matched the ledger was still done by hand. Farhan built recommendation systems for Instagram Reels at Meta, joining billions of raw events to the numbers the business reported. Mazin built trading systems at Optiver, then agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where analysts would not act on a number they could not trace. In finance that work is at least funded. In companies that make and move things, nobody had built it at all.

content.description:
We build foundational AI models for chemistry. Almost nothing you buy is a single chemical. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs.

Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and error in a lab.

Our models predict how a mixture will behave far faster than the standard methods used today, which lets us design new formulations in weeks rather than years, at a fraction of the cost. To prove this, we used them to invent three chemicals that never existed before, including a PFAS-free coolant for datacenters, and we have since synthesized and patented all three.

We are already working with some of the largest manufacturers to design formulations for them, and we are building our own lab to generate the data that will train our next models.

Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. By designing our satellites with zero ITAR/EAR-controlled content, we can leverage manufacturers anywhere in the world to produce our satellites at under a tenth of the cost and launch them from other nations to bypass capacity bottlenecks and access equatorial orbits. 

We're starting off by selling connectivity to device OEMs and network operators, but will eventually use the distributed compute across our constellation to run low-latency inference for robots and autonomous vehicles in remote and rural areas anywhere on the planet.

We've already signed hundreds of millions in LOIs to work with operators across Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, booked our first satellite launch next year, and hold an 11,000 satellite filing with the ITU to build the largest comms network outside of the U.S. and China.

content.description:
Physical AI — robots and world models — is bottlenecked on one thing: diverse,
real-world data at massive scale showing how humans actually do work in the
physical world. It was never written down, and you can't buy it, because no one
has ever captured it. Only real local experts, the people who do this work every
day, can produce data this authentic and valuable.

DeepReach builds the network that reaches them. We design and manufacture
wearable stereo capture devices, then place them with local data partners who
run collection as their own business — in warehouses, workshops, farms, kitchens
and repair shops. They own the local relationships; we supply the hardware, the
software platform, the quality pipeline and the payments. Anyone can run a data
business.

That structure is what produces diversity. Instead of thousands of hours inside
one environment, we deliver hours spread across thousands of environments —
which is what actually makes robot policies generalize.

475 devices in the field and 100+ data partners are live across 7 countries, adding new
partners every week. They've collected nearly 150,000 clips in the past three
months, with volume roughly doubling month over month. Our data is in production
with multiple frontier model and robotics companies, and we're scaling to
10,000+ devices across 50 countries.
content.products_or_services: Network for Physical AI Data Business

content.description:
Orchestra is an inference cloud. We capture your AI work traces, train smaller models, and automatically deploy them (only when they outperform the expensive model you are currently paying for).

Instead of renting the same frontier model forever, your AI infrastructure gets faster, smarter, and cheaper every time it runs.

Suppose your product uses Claude for a repetitive legal workflow.

Orchestra observes successful production runs, learns the specific tools and judgment required for that workflow, and trains a specialized open-weight model.

Once that model matches or beats Claude on a held-out evaluation, Orchestra starts routing production traffic to it.

As more work is completed, the model keeps improving.

We started Orchestra because we believe every company using AI should be accumulating intelligence, not accumulating API bills.

Order to cash is a $60B outsourced function because the work is too messy for traditional automation. Every customer has different context, exceptions do not follow clean rules, and the next step is often buried in emails, portals, handoffs, or someone’s memory. Rex agents run continuously in the background and resolve work to SLA standards so cash keeps moving. We founded Rex after spending four years building Sequence, an a16z-backed finance ops platform, from zero to Series A — where we saw firsthand that at-scale, O2C still runs on manual labour.

Rex is the #1 winner of the Vercel AI Accelerator out of 2,500 teams, selected by Guillermo Rauch and leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Browserbase and more.

content.description:
A new agent, tool, or generative model alone doesn’t solve the whole problem for most research questions. Someone still has to assemble the data, work out which methods to use and get the tools and datasets working together. We’re building Noto, a multiplayer discovery workbench for human and agentic scientists, to bring everyone's favorite frontier models, agents, tools, and scientific models into one shared workspace, so that you can focus on making your next discovery, rather than wrestling with your Python environment or finding GPUs.

Plan an experiment, work with its generated data, run an analysis or model, maybe even train a new model, and keep the results in the notebook. We designed Noto so that the inputs, code, methods and results stay connected across local and hosted compute. Both people and agents need to see how a result was produced and build on it. Biology is where we’re starting, with the workbench being built for more general research across many scientific disciplines.

Available now: our first biological analysis tools, hosted model inference, and an initial agent interface. Free usage is available within limits, alongside paid model runs and individual and team plans. Researchers can run sequence and structure analyses and hosted scientific models without provisioning GPUs or maintaining each model’s dependencies.

In development: the full multiplayer notebook and wider agent workflows and integrations.

Orikata Bio Public Benefit Corporation, or Orikata Bio PBC, is the company. We work under two brands: Orikata Bio for biological discovery and Megure Labs for scientific software.

Biological discovery with Orikata Bio

We’re developing Ibuki, a world-model family for biology, to learn how evolution, sequence, structure and function relate and use those relationships to understand and engineer living systems. We’re pretraining our own protein language models, and developing coordinate and multimodal models for prediction, inverse folding, alignment and generative design. Proteins are our starting point; DNA, RNA, small molecules, and other biological modalities are part of the longer-term direction.

Along the way, we assembled Umi, with over 100 billion unique protein sequences, and Sora, with nearly two billion protein structure records. Having that much data only helps if we can organize it, compare it and find the biology relevant to a particular question. We’re building the full-corpus embedding, indexing and customer access that will bring more of those collections into research workflows.

Our key insight was that the fixed substitution tables used to compare biological sequences are the simplest example of a neural network. Replacing them with contextual substitution operators lets us learn how positions correspond, from reference alignments and directly from molecular geometry. Hikoboshi (open source) turns those learned relationships into tools for sequence and structure alignment, search, clustering and many other evolutionary analysis pipelines.
GitHub: https://github.com/orikata-bio/hikoboshi

Scientific software with Megure Labs

Learning those relationships meant making the alignment calculation itself trainable. Orihime (open source), our differentiable-alignment and structured-attention library, lets neural networks learn through scientific algorithms on CPUs and GPUs. It supplies the training machinery behind our learned alignment methods.
GitHub: https://github.com/megure-labs/orihime

Running the models efficiently is its own problem. Hataya (private evaluation), our inference engine and compiler for scientific models, turns trained models and their dependencies into standalone CPU and GPU programs, carrying the exact weights, identity and verification evidence with them. We’re building it to make both our models and public scientific models cheaper to run, including through Noto’s hosted service.

Kaname coordinates long-running agent work across every model provider: tasks, compute, permissions, retries and the record of what happened. We’re bringing that coordination and provenance into Noto’s research workflows so work can continue across people, agents and machines.

Researchers can start with a single analysis or hosted model run today. Noto is where we’re bringing them together so an analysis or model run can become part of a continuing research project, with the data, methods and results kept alongside it.

Try Noto’s live tools: https://megure.ai/noto/workspace/
Biological tools: https://orikata.ai/tools/
Scientific software: https://megure.ai/
Biological discovery: https://orikata.ai/
Open source: https://github.com/megure-labs and https://github.com/orikata-bio
For research use, questions about the data or private evaluations: casey@orikata.ai

Donkey is the AI-native trading company. Upload a buying list and we land the whole container at one locked, delivered price, tariffs included. You buy from Donkey: one contract, one company responsible for everything between the factory floor and your door. Our own people check the cartons before the factory gets paid, and the balance is due when the goods are accepted at your dock.

Small businesses buy imports through three or four middlemen, each adding 15 to 30 points, because none of them can fill a container on their own. Big enough to buy pallets, never big enough to buy the box. Quotes float with freight, FX and tariffs and live 15 to 30 days.

A trading company is rooms of people on the phone with factories, forwarders and brokers. Donkey runs that as one engine. It finds the real factory behind the customs record, stacks duty line by line, packs the container on weight and cube, and returns one number that holds from signature. Next comes the shared container: small buyers fill one box together at container prices, and every container earns better factory terms for the next one.

Team in San Francisco and Wuhan, English and Mandarin. If your business buys pallets of anything imported, send us your buying list.

content.description:
We want to bring AI agents to a billion people.

To do this, we believe it needs to be 1. proactive and 2. personal. A billion people already carry the right device, but none of them have the right connector.

Moonshot is personal intelligence that lives on your iPhone and listens to you 24/7. It continuously builds up a greater understanding of you through constantly listening and building context. It just pays deep attention, the way a good friend does. Through this, Moonshot monitors your conscious and subconscious life, figuring out what you need before you know, reminding you about open loops, identifying life and emotional trends before you recognize it, and covering a lot more of what we gloss over in daily life.

For fifty years, software has waited to be asked. We think tools are just good enough to flip this, and the next great software will provide value before asking for something first. We're doing it through Moonshot.

Our thesis is simple: you're only living half your life. The half that you actively remember. The other half just evaporates into your subconscious: what you said, felt, promised, and forgot. It's the more interesting half, and until now nothing could catch it, making it not actionable.

Moonshot catches your subconscious half and understands you well enough to take actions on your behalf.

Take life personally.

The iOS app is designed around ambient listening and clear user control. Short microphone chunks are sent securely to Moonshot's private transcription service and deleted when transcription finishes. Text and selected context can be sent through Moonshot's server to a model when the app needs to understand a moment. Nothing leaves without your yes. The privacy policy explains every data path, stored copy, permission, and deletion control in detail.

Moonshot is in early access. Join the waitlist to hear when access opens, read more about the team and product on the About page, or use the Contact page for a direct written response from the Moonshot team.

Let's make it a Moonshot.

content.description:
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once.

Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing.

Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call.

Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point

content.description:
Current is an opinionated way to work with your coding agents. It lets you run hundreds of agents while staying in control.

The problem with running agents in parallel isn't their intelligence. It's your attention. You end up scrolling walls of text and tool calls, looking for answers you'd already been given.

So Current drops the chat entirely and focuses on your agents' outputs, not their inputs. Everything is an issue, from a quick fix to a big project with sub-issues. You write it, and your agents pick it up and deliver.

Current is built with Current. It's free on Mac, Windows, Linux and iPhone, and works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and many more agents.

Masterpiece provides short term working capital to data vendors that sell training data, evaluation work, and reinforcement learning environments to frontier AI labs.

A major financing gap exists in this market. Data vendors often need to pay contributors and fund operations before a lab has completed QA, accepted the work, and paid the invoice. This creates a 30 to 90 day cash gap between when vendors incur costs and when they receive payment. Legacy invoice lenders have little visibility into how to underwrite these assets.

Masterpiece closes that gap by advancing capital against high quality lab contracts and invoices. Vendors can use the capital to scale delivery, pay contributors, and fund growth, then repay masterpiece when the lab payment arrives.

content.description:
In investment management, every decision gets graded. The market prints the answer on a date known in advance, and nobody gets to argue with it.

Kimpton is financial AI that answers to reality. Kimpton OS is the AI-native operating system for investment teams: it does the research and hands PMs structured trades. EarningsBench is a public benchmark where models forecast quarterly earnings before companies report and the reported numbers do the scoring. Koliseum is the set of point-in-time financial environments we build from that work, for labs to train and evaluate models on.

The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade.

Kimpton OS goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions, connects to the institutional data the fund already runs on, and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss.

That same work is how we grade AI. Static benchmarks leak into training data. Simulations reward what their authors imagined. A forecast sealed before the outcome exists and scored when the company reports can't be rehearsed or backdated. We started in markets because they're the one place reality answers on schedule.

We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund, raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We learned to trust live results over historical fit. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack.

We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager. Our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B, and the labs that need to know whether their models can do this work.

At Litmus, we’re building evals for humans and redefining how talent is evaluated. Teams like Mercor, Wispr, Composio, Neo Scholars, Astranis, and more are already using Litmus to build their technical teams.

Every company in the world will soon be powered by neo-humans (agent assisted people). But building evals to measure neo-human performance is unexplored and difficult. It requires systematically benchmarking neo-human capabilities and failure modes across all sectors of knowledge work, developing reproducible environments that test neo-human performance on complex tasks, and designing causal attribution frameworks over execution trajectories to identify and validate reproducible action sequences and decision patterns that lead to successful outcomes.

At Litmus, we’re solving this problem. We deliver hiring insights to companies by capturing how candidates use tools, reason, and make decisions in their interviews, giving agentic graders the evidence to evaluate candidate skillset and predict job performance.

content.description:
The problem: 
AI has quietly become one of the largest and fastest-growing line items for companies. Spend is scattered across a dozen provider consoles that each show one number at the end of the month and nothing about why it moved. There's no unified view, and no way to trace a dollar back to the customer, feature, team, or even the pull request that caused it.

Which customers are unprofitable once you subtract their AI costs? Which feature is quietly burning your Anthropic budget? Is this week's spike a runaway loop or real growth? How much did that AI-written PR actually cost to ship?
Today teams reverse-engineer answers by exporting CSVs from each provider and stitching them together in a spreadsheet, and by the time they do, the money is already spent.

What SuperPenguin does: SuperPenguin tracks AI spend across 14 providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Modal, Cursor, OpenRouter, and more).

* Zero-code setup: connect an API key and costs sync automatically with model-level breakdowns, trends, and forecasts
* Per-request attribution: add two lines with our Python or TypeScript SDK to tag every AI call by customer, feature, team, or environment (or any other metadata).
* AI coding cost per PR: connect Cursor to see engineering spend attributed to each pull request, repo, and developer, so you know what it actually costs to ship.
* Alerts on budget thresholds and spend anomalies, delivered to Slack, email, or Discord.

Most teams are set up in under five minutes. We help companies see where their AI money goes and whether it's worth it.
content.products_or_services: AI Cost Management: Track and attribute AI spend across every provider

Foreman is the all-in-one AI-powered project management platform built for construction contractors and the trade industry.
Today, contractors run complex businesses on a patchwork of tools that were never designed for construction — estimates in spreadsheets, plans in email, proposals copy-pasted from old Word docs, photos scattered across phones. Nothing talks to anything else, and the admin work never stops.
Foreman replaces that patchwork with a single platform that manages the full lifecycle of a construction job, from first estimate to final invoice. Contractors upload plans, photos, or a project description, and Foreman's AI instantly generates structured takeoffs, scoped estimates, and professional proposals — in minutes, not hours. From there, every customer record, document, permit, photo, change order, and conversation lives in one place, organized around the job.
The result: contractors spend less time buried in admin and more time building. They bid faster, manage jobs with less chaos, and close projects cleanly — without duct-taping five tools together to do it.

AI-powered drug discovery is flooding the pipeline with new candidates faster than ever. Our AI-native platform automates it, giving drug developers the confidence to advance the right candidates and stop the wrong ones early.

We have strong commercial traction with enterprise pharma customers. Our founding team built the field of next-generation protein characterization out of Carolyn Bertozzi's Nobel laureate lab at Stanford. Collectively, we have 18+ years of collective domain expertise, 47+ scientific publications, and a 2x YC Founder. We move at the highest velocity and are positioned to lead the next generation of modern AI development in the life sciences.

content.description:
Corvera (YC W26) is the AI sales agent for CPG brands. We turn the data a brand already has into the actions its sales team takes today.

A CPG brand sells into tens of thousands of independent US stores through dozens of distributors, and works that base with a handful of people. CLEAN Cause, a $20M yerba mate brand, covers 21,000 stores through 46 distributors with a four-person sales team. The accounts worth a call are not capped by headcount. The team is.

CLEAN Cause now runs its daily sales decisions on Corvera: 5,000 queries in 40 days across 12 users, $250K of opportunities surfaced within days, and a 7x return on the analysts they would otherwise hire.

With Corvera in place, every sales rep starts the morning with:
- The stores to act on today, ranked and priced, with the reason on the row,
- The outreach already drafted to the right contact at the right distributor, and
- The follow-up booked, logged, and measured against the goal it was set to move.

All from the distributor feeds, retailer portals, and ERP data they already have, resolved into one context layer - without a data team, and without handing their sales to a broker.

We’re founded by Chris (2x Founder; ex-CEO at Better Nature; Forbes 30U30) and Dirk (ex-Google Data & AI Lead).

To date, we’ve raised $6.2M and are backed by YC, firstminute capital, 6 Degrees Capital, 20VC, Rebel Fund, Duke Capital Partners, and more. Our ICP is US CPG brands doing $20M+ in retail revenue through UNFI, KeHE and DSD distributors. We sell to VPs of Sales and CEOs.

The incumbents prove the scale. Brokers take 5-12% of a $350B US independent grocery market, and Advantage Solutions, a publicly traded company, does $3.5B in annual revenue.

Our mission is bold: to enable the next generation of unicorn CPG brands to be run by teams of less than 10 people.

Our vision is even bolder: to give every CPG brand the coverage of a full sales team at a fraction of the headcount, and displace the broker network that covers the US independent channel today.

Visit www.corvera.ai to learn more!

content.description:
Ndea is building frontier AI systems that blend intuitive pattern recognition and formal reasoning into a unified architecture.

# AI for Scientific Advancement

Unlike all life before us, humanity's ascent is a story of ingenuity, not just biological evolution. Our progress has been driven by the curiosity to acquire knowledge, the ability to pass it on, and an intrinsic drive to innovate. We build technology which gives us leverage beyond our biology.

We stand at the top of a knowledge and technology colossus that we collectively created over the past ten thousand generations. Scientific progress has helped us overcome burdens that long defined human life — famines, plagues, and widespread illiteracy. Science will continue to redefine the boundaries of the human condition.

Today, the acceleration of scientific progress hinges on one factor: AI capable of independent invention and discovery. This capacity is the gateway to advancements beyond our wildest imagination.

# A New Research Lab

We're starting Ndea — an AI research and science lab. The name - like 'idea' with an 'n' - is inspired by the Greek concepts ennoia (intuitive understanding) and dianoia (logical reasoning), capturing our first goal to merge deep learning with program synthesis.

Ndea is entirely focused on developing and operationalizing AGI to realize unprecedented scientific progress in our lifetime for the benefit of all current and future generations.

Building AGI alone is a monumental undertaking, but our mission is even bigger. We're creating a factory for rapid scientific advancement — a factory capable of inventing and commercializing N ideas.

From our vantage point today, we see many 'known' frontiers like self-driving vehicles, drug discovery, sustainable energy, robotics, and space exploration. While AGI will benefit all of these, the most exciting adventure lies in the 'unknown'. AGI promises discoveries and progress we cannot imagine today.

content.description:
Moss is building the real-time semantic search runtime for conversational and multimodal AI. Our system enables voice agents, copilots, and chat interfaces to retrieve, reason, and respond in sub-10 ms, delivering the responsiveness that makes AI interactions feel truly natural.

If you’ve ever built a conversational or voice AI product, you’ve felt the lag. That moment when an agent pauses and the illusion of intelligence breaks. The bottleneck is almost always retrieval. Each query hops across networks and databases, adding delay and cost. Moss eliminates that gap by keeping retrieval close to where the agent runs.

Moss runs natively across browsers, mobile devices, and servers with an optimized vector index built in Rust and WebAssembly. It enables teams to build AI products that feel instant, contextual, and adaptive. The experiences that sustain engagement and unlock new kinds of interaction. For our customers, this translates into tangible business value: stronger user retention, higher conversion, and entirely new product categories made possible by real-time understanding. Moss is already powering production pilots across voice AI and developer platforms, achieving sub-10 ms retrieval and 70–90% token savings compared to traditional pipelines.

DiligenceSquared delivers AI-powered market due diligence for investment decisions - like the $500k McKinsey reports, but automated, auditable, and at a fraction of the cost.

Our AI agents conduct expert interviews and synthesize insights with every claim linked to source transcripts. No black box, no "trust me" slides, and no 10x mark-up for human labor.

Frederik bought these reports as a Principal at Blackstone. Soren sold them as a Principal at BCG. Harshil is a repeat founder and former Software Engineer at Google. We've seen both sides and know what matters in due diligence - and now we automate it.

Our clients already include 8 leading private equity funds with over $2.4 trillion in combined AUM.

content.description:
Sourcebot is an open source code understanding platform for massive codebases. We’re used by thousands of engineers in some of the largest companies in the world, including NVIDIA, Red Hat, Wikimedia, and Arista Networks.

Understanding code, not writing it, is the primary bottleneck for large engineering teams. For developers, this means onboarding onto complex codebases faster. For AI agents, it means getting the necessary code context to minimize hallucinations and maximize cohesion within the wider codebase.

Sourcebot solves this by giving developers and AI agents the ability to regex search across millions of lines of code instantly, as well as ask questions across thousands of repos using any flagship reasoning model. Being open source and on-prem, we can get deployed in enterprises within minutes before other tools even get approval.

We met a decade ago at McGill University and have been building together full time for over 2 years. We’ve personally felt the pain of understanding large codebases while working at Microsoft, EA, Ubisoft, Google, and Meta.

content.description:
Aside is an AI browser that completes real work across the websites you already use. It can sign in through your browser, work inside email, dashboards, internal tools, docs, and spreadsheets, and keep going when a task takes minutes or hours.

Unlike agents that depend on integrations, Aside uses the web the way you do. Browsing history becomes local memory, so it knows which tools and context matter. Its password manager lets agents autofill credentials without exposing secrets to the AI. Sensitive actions like payments, posts, and messages wait for your approval.

We achieved state-of-the-art on agentic browsing benchmarks, surpassing OpenAI and Anthropic's result- Aside ranked #1 across Mind2Web, Odyssey, bu-bench-v1.

Imagine AI is a research and software company reverse engineering modern B2B growth, starting with LinkedIn.

As companies get more automated, more of B2B growth will happen between agents, and the companies that connect will compound each other's output. We're building the connective layer between them. We start with content because it's still the fastest way to build B2B relationships at scale.

Today our content agent decides what your team should post based on data from 1M+ people (who posts what, who engages, where they work and how they're connected). It drafts the posts and graphics, schedules them for your execs and company page, and maps engagement back to your pipeline.

Rippling, MarqVision, Slash, Corgi and Fondo use Imagine AI. Customers have generated $40M in revenue, 100M impressions and 14,341 MQLs.

Free public benchmark of how 1,000+ B2B companies and their execs perform on LinkedIn: https://benchmark.useimagine.ai

Pixley turns kids' drawings and ideas into fully animated cartoons – in minutes.

Kids are natural storytellers. With Pixley, any kid can draw a character, describe a world, and watch their story come to life as a personalized animated cartoon.

Every episode is safe, ad-free, and built around Social-Emotional Learning (SEL). We're building the creative platform for the next generation – where kids are the directors, not just the audience.

Additionally, the same technology powers Pixley Studios, our B2B content service for brands and content creators who want to produce high-quality AI video without the cost or time of traditional production.

We’re 19 year old CS dropouts who’ve known each other since elementary school and won 4 hackathons at 15. After seeing AI flood the internet with low-quality content, we created Pixley – a safe, personalized way for kids to turn their ideas into animated stories.

content.description:
Cortex AI builds the world’s most diverse and large-scale real-world workplace robot & egocentric dataset — where the physical world becomes the next training and evaluation set for embodied AI.

We power frontier labs developing robotics foundation models and general-purpose robots by providing the data they need:

Frontier is first to grow biological brains at scale, serving biological neural nets with substrate-level colocation of memory and compute, enabling highly cost effective training of large parameter count models.

While academia has traditionally been limited to ~1M neurons in vitro, Frontier has built a pathway to scale to 100M+ neurons by circumventing traditional scaling challenges in biological culture, demonstrating this strategy's functionality by training a biological brain using this scaling primitive to play Frogger.

Frontier is now growing exascale compute clusters to produce substrates capable of long-horizon language reasoning while operating at much higher sample efficiencies than traditional architectures, and collocating memory with compute to enable significantly larger parameter counts than would be tractable for training within traditional compute clusters.

content.description:
Compyle is a less autonomous coding agent that asks before it acts. We're like Cursor or Claude Code - but you won't need to rewrite your codebase every time you use it for more than a small task.

We built Compyle because we were frustrated with the direction other coding agents are headed. They're all racing to be more autonomous, running for hours without human input.

This doesn't work for real production code. When agents run autonomously, they make countless small decisions that pile up in your codebase. Engineers lose ownership - they don't know what was implemented, can't effectively debug or maintain it, and struggle to build on top of it. The code becomes a black box, and they're forced to throw it away.

Compyle keeps engineers in the driver's seat.

content.description:
Nessie is shared context for all of your AI tools. It automatically syncs your conversations and agent sessions from ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Perplexity and 20+ other tools into one place, so you, your team and your agents can search and build on everything you've worked through with AI.

If you use more than one AI tool, you know the problem. Claude doesn't know what you decided in ChatGPT. Codex doesn't know what Claude Code already tried. Every new session starts from zero. With Nessie, you can ask any agent what you decided about a project, what you already tried for a bug, or what a teammate concluded last week, and it answers from your actual history.

Install the app on Mac, Windows or Linux and connect your AI tools, plus meeting and note apps like Granola, Read AI, Plaud and Obsidian. Nessie keeps syncing in the background, and agents reach it through our MCP server, CLI and plugins.

For teams, Nessie turns everyone's AI work into shared knowledge. Share sessions with a teammate or the whole team, and every agent starts from what the team already knows: what was decided, what was tried, and why. Nessie is SOC 2 certified and runs as SaaS, on-prem or BYOC.

For leaders, Nessie is observability across every AI tool your team uses, not one vendor's dashboard. See which skills and workflows actually succeed, what each one costs, and who is getting results, then double down on what works. That's ROI measured on outcomes, not just tokens.

Where we're going: AI-native companies will run thousands of agents that are powerful but forget everything. Science has journals, law has case law, software has git; AI-native knowledge work has had nothing. Nessie is that shared memory, and it gets better as your company's own history grows.

Founded by two Yale CS grads and former Amazon engineers in San Francisco. Backed by BoxGroup, Pioneer Fund, Y Combinator, Precursor, and more.

content.description:
We analyze every conversation between your customers and your AI agent to find what's losing you customers and money. Then we help ship the fix and prove it worked.

Nobody on the team can read every conversation once an agent is in production. TCC does, and turns them into patterns tied to the accounts they affect: where customers get stuck, what they wish the agent could do, and where it's spending more than it needs to.

Engineers ask about a pattern from their IDE through our MCP, get the conversations and traces behind it down to the tool call or prompt that went wrong, ship the fix, and benchmark cost and quality before and after. Product sees what customers are actually trying to do with the agent and where it falls short, broken out by topic and account, which becomes the backlog for what to build next. Customer success sees which accounts the agent is struggling with before the customer says anything, and steps in with the full conversation on hand.

Any agent framework, a few lines of code. If you're running an agent in production or about to launch, ping us.

The machine economy is coming, and Locus (YC F25) is building the connector businesses will need to participate. We connect agents securely to funds, letting you define permissions and limits for every transaction. Each payment is traceable, auditable, and fully reconcilable with your existing financial stack.

Better drawings build a better world. #GetStructured

content.description:
AI changed coding when it got its own environment instead of a chat window. Developers stopped typing every line and started handing off whole tasks. The phone is next, and it needs the same rebuild.

Blue is that rebuild: a phone that’s also your chief of staff. It reads every notification, text, and email for you. Then it either handles each one and leaves you an FYI, or drafts a reply and waits for your OK. Anything else is one button away: say what needs doing, and Blue gets it done in the background, using the right apps.

It knows you from day one. Switch from your iPhone and Blue brings over your apps, messages, photos, and passwords, so it already knows who matters to you, how you write, and which card to use. No logins to hand over, no context to explain.

An app can’t do this; it takes owning the phone. Blue runs our own OS on Google Pixel today, with our own hardware in development. We sold out our first batch at YC’s Alumni Demo Day in September.

The team brings complementary experience at scale: Omar Abdelaziz led Google Assistant’s transition to LLMs and holds one of the earliest patents in LLM-based computer control; Peter Krogh spent decades designing voice-first dialog systems and before Blue was a design lead at Google DeepMind building actions for Gemini Live; Muhammad Farhan Hossain helped ship Apple Vision Pro, is named on dozens of hardware and systems patents, and has led products from prototype to mass production.

We’ve built systems used by billions. Now we’re building the phone that comes next.

content.description:
Food Supply Chain companies have been using legacy ERPs for decades. Everyone knows these are necessary evils that essentially run the business but take up a lot of operational capacity. They are not about to just rip and replace their existing system that runs their whole business with a system that takes years to implement. Imagine if they could implement AI that runs the ERP for them, in weeks?

Burnt’s building an agentic OS for the Food Supply Chain with AI Agents for each department. 

Our AI Agent, Ozai, has started by replacing the whole order management job function at food distribution companies, so that sales and customer service teams can focus on what matters - the customer. Ozai monitors all incoming messages (emails, phone calls, voicemails, whatsapp, fax etc.), figures out if it's an order, learns each customer's habits, shorthand, and favorite products, picks up on any prep notes, and enters it straight into the existing ERP. It'll even go back to the customers on your behalf when it's not sure about something, clarify things and carry on working. 

The more it sees, the smarter it gets.

Mistakes run rampant, and each mistake is thousands of dollars. Even the select fleets using algorithms that have fleet-wide context struggle: the outputs are rigid, hard to interpret, and are blind to real-world nuances like driver preferences and schedule exceptions. Fleetline solves this by combining advanced optimization with LLMs that can easily adapt algorithms to each fleet’s needs and capture driver-specific information. The result is smarter planning truly optimized for every fleet and its drivers.

Rebulk builds AI-native software for railroads, transload terminals, bulk trucking companies, industrial plants, and commodity merchants.

Much of this industry still relies on spreadsheets, paperwork, manual data entry, and disconnected legacy systems. Teams spend hours on repetitive administrative work, tracking down information, and coordinating operations across different systems. Rebulk brings these workflows together, automates manual processes, and gives businesses real-time visibility into their operations.

We’ve lived this problem, and we know how to build for it. Warren previously led product at a Series A supply chain software startup, where he worked closely with companies moving and managing bulk commodities. Cole was engineer #3 at Tropic, helping scale it from seed to Series B, and later led engineering at an AI startup.
